narrative:
The model estimates a 42% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, your 11+ years of total professional experience was the strongest influence pushing the prediction toward leaving. While only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this much experience, the model sees long overall careers as a sign you may be ready for bigger opportunities elsewhere. Second, the number of training programs you attended in the last three years pulled the prediction back toward staying; attending 7 or more is less common among those expected to remain, and the model views this investment as a positive anchor to the organization. Third, your 1–5 years in your current role added another push toward leaving. This shorter tenure here, compared with longer stays among those predicted to stay, suggests you may still be evaluating whether this is your long-term home.

Taken together, your extensive background and relatively recent start with the company outweighed the stabilizing effect of your many training sessions, tipping the balance toward a higher risk of departure.

The organization should discuss your career goals openly and explore whether additional responsibilities or clearer advancement paths could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying more attractive before deciding on your next step. (218 words)
